anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Mis-tuned runtime settings (memory pool sizes, checkpoint cadence, log sizing, parallelism limits, etc.) that are out of line with hardware capacity or workload requirements.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Total memory consumption by caches, work areas, sessions, and background heaps exceeds the safe physical envelope, provoking OS pressure, paging, or OOM events.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Physical storage devices reach or exceed their sustained IOPS / throughput / latency budget, creating long I/O queues and elevated read-write latency.

When these three root causes strike together, the instance shows a multifaceted degradation: 1) memory pressure and paging explode while the buffer pool and work areas are simultaneously under- or over-provisioned by faulty parameters; 2) log-write and data-file waits rise sharply because storage is saturated, yet wait profiles are further distorted by aggressive checkpoint cadence or oversized parallelism invoking extra I/O; 3) CPU utilization alternates between idle (while sessions stall on I/O) and spin-heavy (while threads contend for starved memory), making capacity metrics contradictory; 4) emergency evictions, failovers, or restarts occur as OOM killers or I/O timeouts are triggered, and recovery is prolonged because both memory availability and disk bandwidth are compromised.

Causally, bad configuration settings can provoke runaway memory allocation—for example, per-session work memory or parallel worker counts that multiply hash/sort buffers—pushing the system into swap and magnifying the Memory Allocation Anomaly. Paging caused by memory exhaustion, in turn, injects extra read/write traffic onto disks that are already near their throughput ceiling, aggravating the Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly. Conversely, saturated storage slows checkpoint and buffer-flush cycles; with mis-set checkpoint intervals or log sizes, dirty pages accumulate, forcing the engine to hold even more memory and to launch emergency checkpoints, which consumes additional RAM and I/O simultaneously. The feedback loop between mis-tuned parameters, escalating memory use, and device-level I/O saturation therefore amplifies each individual problem, rapidly degrading both transactional and analytical workloads until the database becomes unstable or unavailable.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that takes more than the specified amount of time; zero disables the timeout.
entry.trigger_condition: A SQL statement runs longer than statement_timeout, measured from command arrival until completion.
entry.workload_impact: The running statement is aborted; when configured, the timed-out statement is logged.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
